name: Touché Amoré
label: Deathwish
lede: Jeremy Bolm ran a fan site for Thursday, then started a band in Los Angeles whose debut lasts eighteen minutes. Nine years later he turned his mother's death into the record that became its most popular.

eras.title: Gas money and a Thursday fan site
eras.text: Jeremy Bolm started Touché Amoré in Los Angeles in 2007 and built it tour by tour, on gas money. By the end of 2009 it had a 7" on No Sleep, an eighteen-minute debut album, and a festival slot Bolm says told him the work was paying off.

years.h: A Thursday fan-site kid starts a band in Los Angeles
years.p: [[Jeremy Bolm|c3401f13-df8b-45f6-bd20-6f91f67d2cd4]] forms Touché Amoré in 2007 and builds it on West Coast tours. Guitarists [[Nick Steinhardt|fa1c73fc-8f3c-492c-8a26-7f974e093ae4]] and [[Clayton Stevens|3be4621b-8c12-4c8c-8617-853d18e1d1e4]] and drummer [[Elliot Babin|275829e0-2d23-4ddd-bb12-087e44481f46]] settle in around him.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the formation to 2007 and puts the first West Coast tours before the 2008 demo. It doesn't say who played bass at the start.

Bolm came to music as a fan. He told Anti-Matter he first got noticed running an unofficial website for [[Thursday|0acae232-d31a-4211-b6d0-6af1b6350274]], and two years later Thursday's Geoff Rickly sings on the band's debut.

years.h: No Sleep Records puts out the first 7"
years.p: The self-titled 2008 demo 7" is the band's first release, after early West Coast tours. Two of its songs, Broken Records and Honest Sleep, get re-recorded for the debut album.
years.xp: The 7" puts Touché Amoré in the orbit of the label that later releases their split with [[La Dispute|2ec89bcc-5bf9-4d2a-ac5e-44b7496d115a]].

years.h: ...To the Beat of a Dead Horse: 11 songs in 18 minutes
years.p: The debut LP on 6131 Records has Thursday's Geoff Rickly on History Reshits Itself and Jeff Eaton of Modern Life Is War on Always Running, Never Looking Back. Steinhardt drew the artwork.
years.xp:
Sources disagree on the date: Wikipedia's band page says June 2009 (through 6131 and Rickly's Collect Records), the album page says August 4, 2009 (6131). Steinhardt also plays bass on the record.

Rock Sound gave it 9/10, and it landed on several best-of-2009 lists.
play: ...To the Beat of a Dead Horse

years.cap: Touché Amoré on a packed floor, October 2009
years.h: Sound and Fury 2009 is where the work starts to pay off
years.p: Bolm names the 2009 Sound and Fury festival as the turning point. It comes in the same year as the debut album.
years.xp: Bolm told Alternative Press that early support tours paid about "150 bucks a night", so the band lived on merch sales and whatever gas money was left.

eras.title: Leak it first, record it in five days
eras.text: With the lineup set, Touché Amoré toured and swapped splits with La Dispute, Pianos Become the Teeth and Make Do and Mend. They leaked their own second album to build a crowd, signed to Deathwish Inc., and cut Parting the Sea Between Brightness and Me in Kansas in five days.

years.h: The lineup stops changing once Tyler Kirby joins on bass
years.p: By 2010 the band is Jeremy Bolm, Nick Steinhardt, Clayton Stevens, Elliot Babin and bassist [[Tyler Kirby|4d8b1b40-f69e-4bf3-a8fb-47ad3e671e45]]. It has not changed since.
years.xp: Alternative Press notes the same five-piece has held since 2010 and that Bolm compares it to a marriage. Wikipedia doesn't give Kirby's exact joining date or say who played bass before him.

years.h: A split with La Dispute starts a long touring partnership
years.p: Touché Amoré and the Michigan band swap songs on Searching for a Pulse/The Worth of the World, out on No Sleep.
years.xp: A 2010 split with [[Make Do and Mend|0270a7d9-848a-41bc-99c0-cd396c970c55]] on 6131 and Panic follows the same year. La Dispute takes them to Europe in 2011.

years.cap: Jeremy Bolm sings into the crowd, July 2010
years.h: The band leaks its own second album
years.p: Before Parting the Sea Between Brightness and Me is out, Touché Amoré put it online themselves, so crowds know the songs when the tours start.
years.xp: Alternative Press describes it as strategy: fans show up knowing the words, and support slots turn into a way into the emo and hardcore revival crowd around [[La Dispute|2ec89bcc-5bf9-4d2a-ac5e-44b7496d115a]] and Balance and Composure.

years.h: Five days in Eudora, Kansas, with Ed Rose
years.p: The band records Parting the Sea Between Brightness and Me live at Black Lodge Recording, aiming for a raw sound.
years.xp: Ed Rose produced, engineered and mixed. Carl Saff mastered.

years.cap: Touché Amoré play a floor show, July 4, 2011
years.h: Parting the Sea Between Brightness and Me lands on Deathwish
years.p: The first album on Jacob Bannon's Deathwish Inc. earns 81 on Metacritic and 9/10 from Rock Sound. Before release, the band shows one piece of the artwork a week on Steinhardt's blog.
years.xp: Amends, Home Away from Here and ~ streamed early. Rock Sound ranked the album No. 6 of 2011.
play: Parting the Sea Between Brightness and Me

years.cap: Touché Amoré at Fluff Fest, Rokycany, Czech Republic, July 22, 2011
years.h: Their first big run overseas, supporting La Dispute
years.p: Touché Amoré support [[La Dispute|2ec89bcc-5bf9-4d2a-ac5e-44b7496d115a]] across Europe from July 27 to August 12, 2011, behind the new record.

years.h: Bolm starts a label inside Deathwish
years.p: Jeremy Bolm launches Secret Voice in 2012 as an imprint of [[Jacob Bannon|d5c2a3e1-a52a-4af6-8e3f-aa2c4dc69af7]]'s Deathwish Inc.. The name comes from what he calls his low speaking register.

years.h: A BBC Radio 1 session, with Jordan Dreyer guesting
years.p: Recorded while touring with La Dispute, the EP has that band's Jordan Dreyer on it. Bolm says recording where the Smiths and Joy Division had played meant something.
years.xp:
Released on Deathwish (DWI136) and engineered by Simon Askew for BBC host Mike Davies. The four songs are ~, Home Away from Here, I'll Deserve Just That and Amends.

Wikipedia dates the release August 14, 2012; the band page says the session was recorded in May.

years.h: Converge takes them through Europe in November
years.p: Touché Amoré tour Europe with [[Converge|fa31e7d4-a03a-4110-98fc-f8826e95ec25]] in November and December 2012, the band of Deathwish founder Jacob Bannon.

eras.title: Thirty, panicking, and on the Coachella bill
eras.text: With Brad Wood producing, Is Survived By pointed the band's short, fast songs at turning 30 and at panic attacks. The tours got bigger, and in 2015 they played Coachella.

years.h: Is Survived By takes on turning 30, with Brad Wood at the board
years.p: Recorded at Seagrass Studio in Los Angeles, the third album on Deathwish is also the best reviewed so far: 87 on Metacritic.
years.xp:
Alternative Press's Scott Heisel called the breakdowns psychological rather than musical. Jon Simmons of Balance and Composure and Julia Blake of Vow guest. Just Exist came out July 30; the tracklist and artwork came July 17.

Alternative Press says the record deals with turning 30 and panic attacks.

years.h: Two splits in one year, with Title Fight and Pianos Become the Teeth
years.p: The one with [[Title Fight|1154d345-8061-4d04-a52a-6214288523ac]] is on Sea Legs. The one with [[Pianos Become the Teeth|7436d471-fdce-42e8-a3cf-c0dc542c8524]] is on Deathwish and Topshelf.

years.cap: Jeremy Bolm at Highfield Festival, August 2014
years.h: A festival summer ends with a first tour of Russia
years.p: In 2014 Touché Amoré play Reading and Leeds in the UK and Pukkelpop in Belgium, then go to Russia in August for the first time.
years.xp: Earlier that year they played SXSW, toured Europe with Birds in Row, and supported AFI in the US. Wikipedia says Bolm's mother died of cancer in 2014.

years.h: Touché Amoré play Coachella
years.p: A Los Angeles hardcore band on the 2015 bill, which Alternative Press cites as a milestone in their rise.
years.xp: The same year they toured Australia with Every Time I Die and released Self Love, a split 7" on Deathwish with Self Defense Family, written and recorded together and produced by Will Yip.

eras.title: The record about his mother, on a new label
eras.text: Jeremy Bolm wrote about his mother's death from cancer, and the band moved from Deathwish Inc. to Epitaph Records to release it. Stage Four became their most popular record.

years.h: Epitaph signs the band for Stage Four
years.p: Exclaim reports Touché Amoré have signed to Epitaph Records for their fourth album.

years.big: I couldn't write about anything else.
q: I couldn't write about anything else.
years.h: Jeremy Bolm writes the album about his mother's death
years.p: [[Brad Wood|58c8c056-4f9a-4a3b-8dd9-69b06bb23c28]] produces Stage Four, about Bolm's mother's death from cancer; the title also counts it as the fourth record. [[Julien Baker|e3bda984-f349-4924-b4b8-f72478bbb3f3]] sings on Skyscraper.
years.xp:
Pitchfork's Zoe Camp compared it to Sufjan Stevens's Carrie & Lowell. Metacritic has it at 84. Bolm told Anti-Matter it became the band's most popular record.

Wikipedia's band page dates the release September 16, 2016; its album page says September 24.

years.h: A thousand shows in, a live double LP at the Regent
years.p: 10 Years / 1000 Shows: Live at the Regent Theater comes out on Deathwish, recorded at the Los Angeles theater.

years.h: Dead Horse X re-records the debut for its tenth birthday
years.p: The whole of ...To the Beat of a Dead Horse is cut again for the anniversary.
years.xp: Bolm told Anti-Matter he swapped a Morrissey reference for a nod to Leonard Cohen once Morrissey's public statements disappointed him.

years.h: Deflector is the first sign of Ross Robinson
years.p: The single comes out September 10, 2019, produced by [[Ross Robinson|df05fc2e-6ff2-4ba1-95b3-ccb7ede14691]].

eras.title: Two albums with Ross Robinson
eras.text: Ross Robinson produced the last two albums, with guests from Andy Hull to Julien Baker and Lou Barlow. Bolm says the sessions were the closest thing to therapy he has had.

years.h: Lament is made at The Bunker in Brooklyn
years.p: [[Ross Robinson|df05fc2e-6ff2-4ba1-95b3-ccb7ede14691]] produces. [[Andy Hull|528476d9-1325-483d-ae1c-faf31511b4ec]] is the only feature, on Limelight; [[Julien Baker|e3bda984-f349-4924-b4b8-f72478bbb3f3]] sings backing vocals on Reminders.
years.xp: Fans got Limelight on a flexi disc mailed in late July 2020. Bolm said he didn't want to write more about grief. Lament made No. 8 on Stereogum's best albums of 2020, and the Reminders video has friends with their pets, including Skrillex and Frank Iero.

years.h: Nobody's debuts live at Outbreak Fest, months before release
years.p: Touché Amoré play the new song at Outbreak Fest in Manchester in 2024. It comes out July 24.

years.cap: Touché Amoré at Rock am Ring, June 2, 2023
years.h: Lou Barlow and a new label for the sixth album
years.p: Made with [[Ross Robinson|df05fc2e-6ff2-4ba1-95b3-ccb7ede14691]] at The Peaky Barnacle in Los Angeles, Spiral in a Straight Line features [[Julien Baker|e3bda984-f349-4924-b4b8-f72478bbb3f3]] and Lou Barlow and is the band's first on Rise Records.
years.xp: Pitchfork's Ellie Kovach praised the hooks; Kerrang! was mixed. Bolm told Anti-Matter the sessions were the closest thing to therapy he has had.

years.h: Riot Fest in Chicago, with two more BBC volumes
years.p: The band announced in April that it would play Riot Fest in September 2025. The year also brings Live on BBC Radio 1: Vol 4 and Vol 5 on Rise.

sources.title: Anti-Matter: In conversation with Jeremy Bolm
